subfield: Condensed matter and materials physics / photovoltaics
motivation: Miyasaka first used organometal halide perovskites as light absorbers in photovoltaic cells (2009). Park demonstrated the first stable solid-state perovskite cell with efficiency near 10% (2012). Snaith showed, at the same time, that these materials carry charge over long distances in a meso-superstructured and then planar thin-film architecture, which revealed that perovskites are excellent ambipolar semiconductors and not merely sensitizers. Their work created a new field of semiconductor physics. The materials are solution-processable, have defect-tolerant electronic structure, strong absorption and tunable band gaps. Power conversion efficiencies have risen from about 4% to over 26% in single junctions, and perovskite-silicon tandems now exceed 33%, beyond the single-junction silicon limit. Synchrotron and neutron studies of their structural dynamics, ion migration and phase stability have deepened our understanding of soft-lattice semiconductors. This discovery is changing light-emitting devices, detectors and the path to low-cost solar energy for the energy transition.
